subject: DPA redline: scoped processing, subprocessor access & on-call ops impact
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@healthsys.com>
To: david.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@healthsys.com
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: DPA redline + runtime isolation request

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo last week — HealthSys leadership is eager to move forward. Legal sent over a few redlines on the DPA (attached) and they want two things cleared before countersign:

1) Scoped processing language that explicitly limits runtime tenants/compute access to our workloads and prevents model retraining/use of inference payloads for product telemetry.
2) KMS key-handling: we asked for a dedicated customer KMS key for encryption at rest of inference logs + an explicit acknowledgement of which subprocessors will have access.
3) On-call/responsibility: the redline asks for a clause that makes Redwood responsible for immediate remediation if a subprocessor causes data exposure during inference.

We know some asks are uncommon — can you route to Product/Security and confirm feasibility and any operational impact (on-call, SOC evidence) by EOD Wednesday? Attaching HealthSys_DPA_Redline_v3.pdf.

Appreciate a pragmatic path — they want to finalize before their year-end procurement window.

Best,
Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Procurement, HealthSys Solutions
attachments: HealthSys_DPA_Redline_v3.pdf

Olga, Priyom — forwarding HealthSys redlines. Key asks: scoped processing (no training/use), dedicated KMS for inference logs, and a liability/ops-oncall clause tied to a subprocessor incident.

Quick asks:
- Olga: is there a supported path to a customer-managed KMS for inference telemetry today? How much ops work to segregate keys/tenants? Also confirm whether our telemetry/telemetry-derived features could be impacted if we honor a full no-retention/no-usage clause.
- Priyom: any legal appetite for a remediation liability tied to subprocessor incidents? We typically limit liability and require evidence paths. If HealthSys insists, what compensating controls or SLA language could bridge?

They need answers by Wednesday EOD — can we get internal signoff/feasibility and a recommended response that balances risk and the procurement timeline?

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: david.kim@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: sara.patel@healthsys.com
Date: 2026-11-19T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline + runtime isolation request

On Wed, Nov 18, 2026 at 10:05 AM David Kim wrote:
> Olga, Priyom — forwarding HealthSys redlines. Key asks: scoped processing (no training/use), dedicated KMS for inference logs, and a liability/ops-oncall clause tied to a subprocessor incident.

David — technical notes below. High level: most asks are reasonable but carry tradeoffs.

1) Scoped processing (no training/use):
- We can add contractual language that prohibits using customer inference payloads for model training or improvement. However, we need to define telemetry exceptions for system reliability (anonymized service metrics). Suggest a carveout for metadata and aggregated telemetry used solely for SRE/quality (not training).
- Impact: disables some automated quality backfills (diagnostics) unless the customer opts into a separate opt-in pipeline.

2) Dedicated KMS for inference logs:
- We support customer-managed keys for data at rest for storage buckets and encryption of persisted logs. For streaming KV cache and ephemeral memory we do not persist keys in the same way — clarify whether HealthSys means persisted logs only.
- Ops effort: provisioning a unique key + key rotation policy is straightforward for Dedicated/Private customers; for Hosted it requires additional onboarding steps and a billing change. Expect ~2–4 week engineering lead time to add cross-account KMS bindings and validate key access logs.

3) Subprocessor/on-call liability:
- We cannot accept open-ended remediation liability for third-party subprocessors. We can commit to:
  - rapid incident response SLAs (e.g., initial triage within 2 hours),
  - forensic evidence sharing subject to NDAs,
  - a commercial remedy limited to incident-related direct costs (capped).
- We can also provide a subprocessor roll-forward list and an attestation schedule (quarterly).

Next steps: I can prepare a short technical annex describing what "no-training" means operationally and a proposed KMS onboarding checklist. If Legal needs stronger guarantees, propose: (a) HealthSys runs in Redwood Dedicated or Private with KMS and (b) an agreed incident response playbook.

Olga
Olga Petrov
Product Security Lead — Redwood Inference
attachments: runtime_isolation_matrix.xlsx

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: david.kim@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: sara.patel@healthsys.com, contracts@healthsys.com
Date: 2026-11-20T08:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline + runtime isolation request

Thanks — quick legal framing and suggested response.

On Thu, Nov 19, 2026 at 11:30 AM Olga Petrov wrote:
> (Olga's technical notes)

Priyom here. We should avoid absolute remediation liability for subprocessor incidents; that creates outsized exposure. Suggested negotiation posture:

- Accept: explicit no-training clause for inference payloads, with a narrowly defined exception for anonymized SRE telemetry. Add a short annex defining allowed metadata fields and the data retention window (90 days by default, configurable).
- Accept with conditions: customer-managed KMS for persisted logs if HealthSys selects Dedicated or Private deployment. For Hosted, offer managed KMS with a contractual attestation and SOC evidence. Include a 30-day onboarding SLA and a one-time integration fee.
- Counterproposal on liability: commit to the incident response SLAs Olga suggested + remedial actions and a commercial cap tied to the MRR value of the account (e.g., 3x monthly committed revenue) rather than open damages. Offer an escrowed list of subprocessors with a 30-day notice period for changes.

I will draft the response language and attach a short redline that preserves our standard limits but offers the commercial cap and KMS path. If Sales wants to be more aggressive, we can drop the cap for Dedicated/Private with a higher seat price.

I'll share the redline in an hour.

— Priyom
Sr. Counsel — Redwood Inference
attachments: redlined_clause_diff.txt

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: sara.patel@healthsys.com, contracts@healthsys.com
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-21T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline + runtime isolation request

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear asks and the redline. Internal summary and proposed path: 

1) Scoped processing/no-training: we can accept a contractual prohibition on using inference payloads for model training. We'll include a short technical annex that defines allowed telemetry (anonymized, aggregated SRE metrics only) and a 90-day retention default.

2) KMS: for persisted inference logs we can support a customer-managed KMS but recommend HealthSys run on Redwood Dedicated or Private for the cleanest integration. For Hosted, we can provide managed KMS with attestation and SOC artifacts; onboarding ~2–4 weeks and a one-time setup fee.

3) Subprocessor/on-call liability: we cannot accept unlimited remediation liability for third-party subprocessors. Our counter:
   - Incident response SLA (initial triage within 2 hours), forensic evidence sharing, and remediation cooperation;
   - Commercial remedy limited to direct incident costs with a liability cap tied to the account (we propose 3x monthly committed revenue);
   - Quarterly subprocessor attestation and 30-day notice on major changes.

Priyom will send the redlined language (attached) and Olga will add the technical annex and a KMS onboarding checklist. If that package works we can get a countersign path started and commit to a procurement timeline that aligns with your year-end window.

Can you confirm HealthSys's preferred deployment (Hosted with managed KMS vs Dedicated/Private with customer KMS) so we can finalize the SOW and timeline?

Thanks — I'll stay on this thread to expedite.

David
David Kim
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
